text: Hey! If you want to learn a little bit more about me outside of my major, your in the right place! Below I have added some of the things that make me who I am. Enjoy!

title: About Me
text:
My Hometown
I grew up in Manhattan Beach, California, which is also more casually known as “The Bubble”! I grew up just a few blocks up from the beach, which is what brought me to love the ocean and inspired me to potentially pursue a career in marine conservation. I will forever love my hometown and am so grateful to have gotten to grow up in such a beautiful place.

title: About Me
text:
My Family






In order left to right: Brother (Marty), Mom, Me, Dad





I grew up in a very loving, supportive family with my mom (Zoya), dad (John) and my little brother Marty (3 years younger). My family is super important to me and they are the reason I am who I am today. Without my mom, I would not know what hard work and dedication was. Without my dad, I would not know what empathy was, or be as caring for others as I am today. Without my brother, I would have been bored out of my mind during COVID, and would not have a soft and loving spot in my heart. One day, I hope to be as fun and free as my parents are. Some of our favorite family activities include playing cards, surfing, road tripping, and bineg watching SNL skits while dying laughing.

The Family Password: Pepper






Pepperoncini Cocoa Matich: our lovely Bernese Mountain Dog





Pepper is the love of my life and the best dog in the entire world. She was the topic of my college personal statement essay, which got me in to so many schools, and our cherished COVID baby. She is also known as: Boom, Booming, Mamas, Peps, Pepsi, and more.

title: About Me
text:
Education + Aspirations
I currently have a focus in Marine Biology and Terrestrial ecology. Some of my career interests are field work and getting involved in marine or terrestrial conservation and restoration work. I am very passionate about sustainability and protecting our natural resources and species
Some upcoming exciting news is that I will be participating in the Bren Fellowship Program this upcoming summer assisting on the “Promoting Wildfire Resilience in Santa Barbara County” project. I was also selected to be published in the 2026 Edition of Starting Lines, the text book for the UCSB writing program.

title: Does harbor activity influence Tridacna maxima giant clam size, density and population dynamics on Heron Island?
text: For my study abroad Marine Biology field course in teh Fall 2025, I went through the entire research process, where in groups we developed a research question and project outline studying Giant Clam ecology in Heron Island. Our group analyzed the differences in size and abundance across a disturbed (near by the island harbor) and undisturbed site on the island.

title: A Translation on Anotation
text:
As my Writing 2 Project 2 in Spring 2025, I developed a podcast script that resembled a conversation between different peer reviewed articles and authors. The topic of interest was the benefit and the downfalls of annotation in preliminary education. As of this past May, this project will be published in the 2026 Edition of Starting Lines, the text book for Writing 1, Writing 2, and Linguistics 3A, 3B, 3C classes
